title: feat(types,plugin-grid)!: object-grid and list-view conditionalFormatting take the spec list view's { condition, style } rule only; the native dialect is refused by name (objectui#11533)
body:
Fixes #11533

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`conditionalFormatting` on `object-grid` (`ObjectGridSchema`, and so the `object-view` `table` slot built from it) and on `list-view` takes ONE rule dialect, the spec list view's `{ condition, style }`. The native `{ field, operator, value }` rule, its `expression` template predicate and a colour written at the top level of a rule (`backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `textColor`) are retired with no alias window and refused by name. This executes triage's ruling `5965301211` (retire, as objectui#11522 ruled for the kanban board in `5963861071`; never widen the spec's list-view member). Stored stock is not authoring: `resolveConditionalFormatting` keeps every arm, so a grid or list view STORED with a native rule still paints, byte for byte as before.

## What changes

| Rule on `ObjectGridSchema`, an `object-view` `table` or a `list-view` | Before (BASE `8bfc0012`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `{ condition, style }` (string, envelope or `''` condition) | accepted on every face | accepted, unchanged |
| native `{ field, operator, value, backgroundColor }` | accepted on every face, tolerant and strict | refused at `field`, `operator`, `value` and `backgroundColor`, each naming the retirement |
| `{ expression, backgroundColor }` | refused as a bare `invalid_union` at the rule | refused at `expression` and `backgroundColor` by name |
| flat CEL `{ condition, backgroundColor }` | refused as a bare `invalid_union` at the rule | refused at `backgroundColor` by name, and `style` (required) |
| `{ condition, style, backgroundColor }` | tolerant faces accepted it (the key was stripped, then painted by the shared resolver anyway); strict face refused it as `invalid_union` | refused at `backgroundColor` on every face |
| `{ condition, style, label }` | tolerant faces accepted it, strict face refused it | refused on every face, `unrecognized_keys` with the spec rule's own message |

The faces read: the `ObjectGridSchema` and `ListViewSchema` mirrors, and `safeValidateSchema` (tolerant) and `StrictAnyComponentSchema` (strict), each on a `list-view` node and on an `object-view` `table` slot. Both columns were read with a throwaway probe on each tree; it was deleted and never committed.

**Not judged here, and unchanged: the authored `object-grid` node's `properties` bag.** Its members are `@objectstack/spec`'s `ComponentPropsMap['object-grid']` row by reference (objectui#11276). The installed 17.5.0 row types `conditionalFormatting` as `unknown`, so the bag accepted all six rules before and after. It carries no objectui copy of the rule, and objectui does not narrow a spec row (see Acceptance notes).

- **zod (`@object-ui/types`, `src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`).** The grid's and the list view's shared rule `ConditionalFormattingRuleSchema` (module-private, one declaration for both mirrors) is no longer a union. It is the spec `ListViewSchema.conditionalFormatting` element (`SpecListViewRuleSchema`, now declared once above the grid mirror and `.extend()`-ed by both this rule and the kanban rule), so it inherits the spec rule's strictness and its `style` map. Two things are layered on top: `condition` stays `SpecRuleConditionSchema` (objectui's `z.string()` arm before the spec slot, so a string is not canonicalized and `''` is still accepted, objectui#10946), and seven retirement tombstones: `field`, `operator`, `value`, `expression`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `textColor`, through a `gridRuleKeyRetired` message builder. The grid member's `.describe()` and the "intentionally broader than spec (migration deferred)" docblock lines go; `conditionalFormatting` leaves that list.
- **TS (`objectql.ts`).** `ConditionalFormattingRule` is an interface that extends `SpecConditionalFormattingRule` and declares the same seven keys `?: never`. `ObjectUIConditionalFormattingRule` is deleted and dropped from the root barrel (TS2305 for an importer). tsc reports each retired key at the key (TS2322).
- **`@object-ui/plugin-grid`.** The `object-grid` registration's `conditionalFormatting` input description stops advertising both forms: it describes the one rule and names the retired spellings. No render path changes.
- **Docs.** A `conditionalFormatting` row in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`'s ObjectGridSchema table; `packages/types/src/zod/README.md` drops the member from the broader-than-spec list.
- **One changeset** (`11533-grid-listview-rule-dialect-retired.md`): `@object-ui/types` and `@object-ui/plugin-grid` `minor`, BREAKING in the first line, before/after table, respelling, the bag and the paint stated as unchanged.

## Mechanism hypotheses, measured

**H1, the faces and the shared union (a type-checker census, not grep).** A TypeScript LanguageService over all 5,034 tracked TS sources, under the root tsconfig's paths (which resolve `@object-ui/types` to source): `findReferences` on each declaration, plus every `conditionalFormatting` identifier resolved to the declaration it binds.

| Declaration | Consumers | How each moved |
|---|---|---|
| zod `ConditionalFormattingRuleSchema` | `ObjectGridSchema.conditionalFormatting` and the `ListViewSchema` override (2 refs); through the grid mirror's `.shape` it also builds the `object-view` `table` slot | all narrow with it. No other zod schema embeds either member: `ObjectGridBlockSchema` takes six other mirror members by reference, not this one |
| TS `ConditionalFormattingRule` | `ObjectGridSchema.conditionalFormatting`, `NamedListView.conditionalFormatting`, the root barrel, the 10946 relay pin, a docblock link in the kanban rule | narrowed in place (same name, now the one-dialect interface) |
| TS `ObjectUIConditionalFormattingRule` | the old union and the root barrel only | deleted |
| `ObjectGridSchema.conditionalFormatting` member (12 refs) | `ObjectGrid.tsx` (5 reads, each handed to the resolver or the harvest as an unknown array), plugin-view's route-2 relay, tests | follows the type; plugin-grid and plugin-view type-check green |
| zod `ListViewSchema` member (10 refs) | `ListView.tsx` (`evaluateConditionalFormatting`'s rules parameter, the harvest, the relay into its grid node), app-shell `ObjectView.tsx`'s relay (its other operand is `any`), tests | follows the type; plugin-list type-check green |
| `resolveConditionalFormatting` | types its own input (`ConditionalFormattingRuleLike` in `@object-ui/core`) | does NOT narrow, by construction |
| `listViewPredicates` (the predicate-field harvest) | reads `readonly unknown[]` | does NOT narrow: it still projects a stored native rule's field |

Can the kanban rule and the grid/list rule become one schema? Measured: same base element (now one declaration), same `condition` arms (pinned arm by arm), same `style` (identity, pinned). They differ in exactly two things: the carrier and card each message names, and `expression`, which the grid and list rule carried and the kanban rule never did (kanban refuses it through the spec's own unrecognized-keys message with its "Did you mean `expression` → `condition`?"). Folding them would change `object-kanban`'s landed refusal text and its `expression` path, a surface objectui#11522's contract record judged on its landing head. Not done here; the report carries the option.

**H2, the census.** Two instruments. (1) An AST pass (TypeScript parser) over the 59 TS files that mention `conditionalFormatting` or `ConditionalFormattingRule`: every object literal with a `field` + `operator` pair, a top-level colour beside a predicate key, or an `expression` beside a style key: 50 hits, each triaged by hand. The filter literals it also caught (`UserFilterTabRuleSchema`, `ReportFilterSchema`, filter fixtures) are its live control. (2) A text pass over every other tracked file that mentions the member: the 500 characters after each token, for a retired key in any syntax: 1 window, the kanban row of the schema reference, which teaches the forms as refused.

| Where | Writers at BASE | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `unmirrored-declared-round6-6152.test.ts` | 1 native (the `valid` row) and 1 native with a wrong operator (the `invalid` row) | `valid` respelled `{ condition: "record.status == 'open'", style: { backgroundColor: '#fee2e2' } }`; `invalid` replaced by `{ condition: "record.status == 'late'", style: 'color: red' }`, because its wrong value (an operator outside the native enum) has no member left to be wrong in |
| `export-options-spec-parity.test.ts` | 1 native (the neighbour-member control) | the native line removed; the control keeps the `{ condition, style }` line and the non-array refusal |
| `objectViewHostSurface.test.tsx` (plugin-view) | 1 forwarding sentinel `{ field, operator: 'eq', value, color }` | respelled `{ condition: "record.stage == 'won'", style: { color: '#ff0000' } }` |
| `gridRowDecorationMembers-8071.test.tsx` (plugin-grid) | 11 rules carrying retired members (the predicate precedence, the colour members) | kept and re-framed as STORED-rule reads; a new block pins refused-at-authoring beside painted-at-render |
| `spec-expression-wire-slots-10946.test.ts` | none; it indexed the union's second arm | reads `condition` straight off the rule's shape |
| `listConditional.test.ts`, `predicate-fields.test.ts` (core) | 10 and 1 | untouched: the resolver's arms and the harvest stay |
| `ConditionalFormattingEditor.test.tsx` (app-shell) | 4 | untouched: Studio's upgrade-on-read of stored rules |
| `kanban-conditional-formatting.test.ts`, `unmirrored-declared-round3-6152.test.ts` | 4 and 3 | untouched: the kanban refusals, and the report component's own rule (a different carrier) |
| plugin-grid registration description | taught both | rewritten |
| objectui `examples/`, `apps/console` non-test code, `skills/` | zero; controls fire (`object-grid` / `list-view` in 5 `examples/` files, `object-grid` in 1 console file and 3 `skills/` files) | none |
| objectstack `examples/` at `4916168` (my own sparse clone) | zero. The one `conditionalFormatting` (app-showcase `field-zoo.view.ts`) is `{ condition, style }`; controls fire (`object-grid` / `list-view` view files, `{ field, operator, value }` filter literals) | none |
| `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` | NOT MEASURED: not in this container. Triage measured zero | none |

**H3, stored rules still paint.** Before and after, through the real `ObjectGrid` and through the real `ListView` handing its node to the real grid, for all six rules of the table: the readings are byte-identical, for example `native: Alpha=[background-color: rgb(1, 2, 3);] Beta=[null]` on both trees and both renderers. Read paths that could validate a stored view: none on the render path (`SchemaRenderer` runs only the dev-only structural `validateSchema`; nothing parses a grid or list-view node). Outside `packages/types`, the only non-test callers of objectui's zod faces are the CLI's `objectui validate` / `objectui check` (authoring doors) and three unrelated schema imports (a dashboard widget, a dashboard designer door, a map config). Studio's `clientValidation` judges a view draft against `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ViewSchema`, not objectui's face, so this change does not reach it; the installed spec's list-view rule already refuses the native rule there (`unrecognized_keys` naming `field`, `operator`, `value`, `backgroundColor`), at BASE as now. Premise held; nothing for the seat.

**H4, the refusals.** One arm, so each refusal sits at the retired key's own path; the messages are byte-identical on the tolerant and strict faces and on both carriers. Quoted, with backticks as in the source:

- at `conditionalFormatting.N.field` (`operator` and `value` the same, key swapped):
  > `field` belongs to the native rule dialect `{ field, operator, value }`, which `conditionalFormatting` on `object-grid` and `list-view` no longer accepts: RETIRED (objectui#11533), with no alias window. A rule is `{ condition, style }` — a CEL `condition` over `record.*` and a CSS `style` map, the rule `@objectstack/spec`'s `ListViewSchema.conditionalFormatting` declares. Respell `{ field: 'priority', operator: 'equals', value: 'high', backgroundColor: '#fee2e2' }` as `{ condition: "record.priority == 'high'", style: { backgroundColor: '#fee2e2' } }` (`not_equals` is `!=`, `greater_than` is `>`, `less_than` is `<`, `contains` is `.contains(…)`, `in` is `record.f in [ … ]`).
- at `.expression`:
  > `expression` is the template predicate of the native rule dialect, which `conditionalFormatting` on `object-grid` and `list-view` no longer accepts: RETIRED (objectui#11533), with no alias window. A rule is `{ condition, style }` — […same sentence…]. Write the predicate as the rule's `condition`, in CEL over `record.*` with no `${…}` wrapper: `{ expression: '${record.amount > 1000}', backgroundColor: '#fee2e2' }` is `{ condition: 'record.amount > 1000', style: { backgroundColor: '#fee2e2' } }`.
- at `.backgroundColor` (`borderColor` the same; `textColor` ends `style: { color }`):
  > `backgroundColor` is a colour written at the top level of the rule, which `conditionalFormatting` on `object-grid` and `list-view` no longer accepts: RETIRED (objectui#11533), with no alias window. A rule is `{ condition, style }` — […same sentence…]. Move the colour into the rule's CSS map: `style: { backgroundColor }`.
- Beside these, a rule with no `condition` also draws `invalid_union` at `.condition` and `invalid_type` at `.style` (both required); an undeclared key draws the spec rule's own message, "Unrecognized key(s) on this conditional formatting rule: `label`. …".

## The pins

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/grid-list-view-conditional-formatting-11533.test.ts` (new, 44 tests): on each of the six faces, the `{ condition, style }` control (string and envelope); the native rule refused at each retired key with the message starting with the key's name and containing `RETIRED (objectui#11533)`, `{ condition, style }` and the respelling, while the accepted rule at index 0 of the same document draws no issue; `expression` refused with its respelling; the flat CEL rule refused at the colour key with no `invalid_union` at the rule; all three colour keys refused beside a `style`; the spec's unrecognized-keys message. The reference: the two mirrors share one rule object, `style` is the spec element's own member (identity), `condition`'s second arm is the spec slot and both arms are the kanban rule's, with the control that `condition` is not the bare slot. The TS face: `@ts-expect-error` on each retired key, on a native rule in an `ObjectGridSchema` and a `ListViewSchema` literal, `keyof` equality with the zod input, and the three members (`ObjectGridSchema`, `ListViewSchema`, `NamedListView`) carrying the one rule.
- `gridRowDecorationMembers-8071.test.tsx` (plugin-grid): the stored native rule refused by `ObjectGridSchema` at `field` with the retirement, AND painted by the real grid on the matching row only; the respelling accepted and painting the same row the same colour as the control.
- `ListView.storedRuleDialect-11533.test.tsx` (plugin-list, new): a stored list view's native rules refused by `ListViewSchema` at `field`, AND handed to its `object-grid` node untouched; the respelling as the control.
- `apps/console/.../registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`: the `object-grid.conditionalFormatting` member-pin prose says the retired members are stored-rule reads now (prose only, no logic).

## Acceptance notes

- **The authored `object-grid` bag.** At the installed spec the bag still accepts any rule, because the spec row's member is `unknown`; objectstack `main` (`4916168`) types it as the list view's own member by reference, so the bag narrows with the `@objectstack/*` bump that carries objectstack PR #21463. Carrier: objectui#11438 (the 17.6.0 trunk) or the bump after it.
- **The skills guide.** `skills/objectui/guides/schema-expressions.md`'s "Legacy shapes are translated" bullet says the native and `expression` forms "still work" under a heading naming list, grid and kanban: true of the evaluator, now false of authoring on all three carriers. `skills/**` is governed and this PR stays ungoverned, so it is left; it is the same item as objectui#11522's contract record escalation (c).
- **The evaluator's native arms** now have no authored carrier on any objectui face; they serve stored rules only. Their removal is the separate act after a stored-stock census, as triage ruled.
- **The report component's own rule** (`ReportComponentSchema.conditionalFormatting`, a `{ field, operator, value, backgroundColor?, textColor? }` shape `ReportViewer` reads per cell) is a separate declaration, and neither spec line declares a report rule member. Untouched. Carrier: none.
- `ROADMAP.md` records the dual-format union as delivered; it is a dated log and is left.
- Files outside the claim's list: `packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx` (comment only: `getCardStyles`' stated reason became false), `ListView.storedRuleDialect-11533.test.tsx` (the H3 pin), `objectViewHostSurface.test.tsx` (sentinel respelled), the console pin prose.
